name: MAR Fund Small Grants Program: Reef Rescue Initiative Window
summary: Annual small grants for science-based coral reef restoration, repopulation and rehabilitation anywhere on the Mesoamerican Reef, including responses to coral bleaching and coral disease.
reporting: Grantees submit the technical, financial, and environmental and social reports required by the grant agreement, on time.

steps: Proposal and due diligence documents via the online system
SGP Grants and Evaluation Committee review, then Board decision

eligibility.rule: The organisation is duly registered or legally recognized in one of the four MAR countries
The organisation is in compliance and good standing as a legal local entity
The organisation is guided by an operational Board of Directors
The organisation has a sound financial management system and structure
The organisation has a good history as a grantee
The organisation has experience in coastal and marine resources management
An individual applicant has administrative support from an NGO responsible for the grant
The proposal does not duplicate funds or efforts funded by other MAR Fund initiatives or programs

documents: Business form, if proposing a sustainable venture or business
Proof of land ownership or legal right to use land, if constructing small infrastructure
Collaboration letters, if collaborating with other local entities
Environmental and Social Screening Tool, for continuity proposals

window.quote: MAR Fund is delighted to announce its Small Grants Program annual request for proposals (RfP) with two available financial windows

co_finance_required.quote: For this RfP, at least 25% of the total budget must come from other sources, as a match to the requested funds.

reporting.quote: submit all required technical, financial, and environmental and social reports on time, according to the grant agreement

amount.quote: The maximum grant amount is US$33,000, based on project needs and capacity of the implementing institution.

effort.quote: Complete proposals and the due diligence documentation, including the signed Appendix B, must be submitted through the on-line form/template on the MAR Fund webpage.
The deadline for the submission of proposals is October 20th, 2026.
Those selected to advance to the next stage will be contacted with instructions to make necessary revisions if required.
Proposals submitted under the RRI window will also be reviewed by the RRI Technical Supervisory Committee (TSC), which will provide technical recommendations.

Project proposals will then be reviewed by the SGP Grants and Evaluation Committee, which will recommend the proposals to be supported in this RfP to be sent to the MAR Fund Board of Directors, who will make the final decision.

eligibility.quote: Be duly registered or legally recognized in one of the four countries of the Mesoamerican Reef (MAR) region (Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, and Honduras);
Be in compliance and good standing with all requirements for operation as a legal local entity;
Be guided by an operational Board of Directors;
Have a sound financial management system and structure in place (accounting, annual audits, etc.);
Have a good history as a grantee (i.e., effective grant/project implementation);
Have experience in the field of coastal and marine resources management.
individuals (who must have administrative support from an NGO to submit the proposal and be responsible for the grant if the project is approved).
proposals involving duplication of funds/efforts funded by other MAR Fund initiatives or programs will not be considered.

co_finance.quote: For this RfP, at least 25% of the total budget must come from other sources, as a match to the requested funds. The match may be both cash and in-kind.

after_award.quote: submit all required technical, financial, and environmental and social reports on time, according to the grant agreement.

documents.quote: Proposal Format - 2026 Annex 1 - Project Development Table - 2026 Annex 2 - Example of indicators - 2026 Annex 3 - Project Budget - 2026

the due diligence documentation, including the signed Appendix B, must be submitted through the on-line form/template on the MAR Fund webpage. Applicants submitting a proposal on the implementation of sustainable ventures/businesses that can demonstrate a positive impact on the natural resources of the MAR must also fill out the business form.
If the proposal includes construction of small infrastructure, the applicant must submit documented proof of land ownership or legal right to use the land at the proposal stage.
For collaborations with other local entities (women's, indigenous peoples, and community groups/organizations, NGO and GO), please provide collaboration letters for the project
You should also attach the due diligence documents that have been modified/updated, the new Project Development Table, the Project Budget, and the Environmental and Social Screening Tool.
